messages:
marie: heads-up — i’m kicking off the RBAC schema refactor next week. plan is: introduce role_permissions_v2, migrate default assignments with a marker, and flip a feature flag `rbac_v2` for routing. posting the canary + rollback checklist here. pls review.

jon: high level looks fine. what’s the backfill approach? any long locks?

sam: avoid any full-table rewrite on the live write path. do shadow-table + chunked copy by `tenant_id` hash, then swap pointer. sample pattern: 
```sql
INSERT INTO role_permissions_v2 (role_id, perm, meta)
SELECT role_id, perm, meta
FROM role_permissions
WHERE id > $last_id
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 5000;
```
Follow with `UPDATE user_roles SET role_ref = new_id WHERE role_ref = old_id` in tenant-scoped batches.

eli: note — migration will touch encrypted `meta` column. we need a KMS key with decrypt allowed for the migration principal. also add key-usage audit so we can trace decrypt calls.

marie: good call. plan to create a dedicated key `projects/redwood/keys/rbac-migration-prod` and limit it to infra:migration role. will open KMS policy PR.

oncall-sec: add fallback in auth middleware: if `rbac_v2` lookup returns empty, fall back to v1 for 30s and increment a metric `auth.fallback.rbac_v1`. if fallback rate > 1% in 5m, auto-rollback (flip flag). also throttle migration writes to avoid auth hot paths.

sam: for default role backfill we must be conservative — we had a previous incident where a default assignment leaked elevated perms to service accounts. include a `source='migration_v2'` tag and skip tenants that have custom default_role set.

jon: can we do canary by tenant? suggest: staging -> prod canary tenant -> 10 small tenants -> full. monitor: 403s, auth latency P95, and failed DB tx. thresholds: 403 increase >0.3% or auth latency +100ms triggers hold.

marie: agreed. will script a dry-run mode that writes to `role_permissions_v2` but never flips `rbac_v2`. include `--dry-run` output and sanity checks.

eli: KMS request: creating key requires sec-ops and infra approval. @oncall-sec please sign off on key policy: restrict to `serviceAccount:infra-migrations@redwood` and require `requester_pays` tag.

oncall-sec: signing off for policy shape, but require audit log gate: every Decrypt/Encrypt must emit `migration_job_id`.

marie: rollback plan in short: 1) flip `rbac_v2` flag off; 2) redirect reads to v1; 3) run reconciliation job to move any partially applied changes back to v1 using `migration_id`; 4) mark `role_permissions_v2` as archived, keep for 30 days. test script attached in PR.

sam: one more: add tight DB timeout on the migration worker (30s) and retry with exponential backoff to avoid holding connections. log full query plan when a batch takes >5s.

jon: add lightweight smoke tests pre/post flip: sample token auth, impersonation check, and a privileged op. automate in release pipeline.

audit-bot: migration_job 1772416789 started by marie. uploading logs to s3://rbac-migrations/1772416789.log. key usage events will be attached.

marie: thank you — creating PRs for migration job, feature-flag gating, KMS policy, and runbook. tagging reviewers: @jon @sam @eli @oncall-sec. will not ship without approvals and canary green. :thumbsup:

oncall-sec: :thumbsup: please add a short post-mortem template to the runbook in case of regressions.

marie: done — runbook includes rollback checklist, monitoring dashboard links, and contact matrix. I’ll post timeline and the exact canary tenants tomorrow.
